nodes.description: Axonal degeneration is the consistent finding in animals lacking alpha-II spectrin, and it falls preferentially on large-diameter myelinated axons, which have the highest density of nodal alpha-II spectrin and bear the greatest mechanical load. In a mouse with a destabilising alpha-II spectrin missense variant at Arg1098, the residue mutated in one SPG91 ataxia patient, heterozygous animals develop progressive ataxia with axonal and dendritic disruption and loss of more than 80% of cerebellar Purkinje cells. No neuropathology from an SPG91 patient exists, so degeneration of the corticospinal tract and of peripheral axons in humans is inferred from these models and from the clinical picture.

nodes.description: In axons, alpha-II/beta spectrin tetramers span the gaps between regularly spaced actin rings, forming the membrane-associated periodic skeleton. This lattice resists the stretching, torsion and compression that long axons undergo and organises the axon initial segment, nodes of Ranvier and paranodes. Removing alpha-II spectrin from sensory neurons in mice breaks this periodic organisation at nodes and paranodes. That SPG91 variants weaken the lattice is an inference from their modelled effects and from loss-of-function models; it has not been shown in SPG91 patient neurons.

evidence.snippet: We analyzed αII spectrin-deficient mice of both sexes and found that, in myelinated axons, αII spectrin forms a periodic cytoskeleton with βIV and βII spectrin at nodes of Ranvier and paranodes, respectively, but that loss of αII spectrin disrupts this organization.

nodes.description: Alpha-II spectrin's N-terminal partial repeat completes a three-helix bundle with the C-terminal helices of a beta-spectrin, which is how two alpha/beta heterodimers join head to head into a tetramer. Arg19 forms a salt bridge with an aspartate on the beta-spectrin helix. The tryptophan substitution is predicted to weaken this interaction, and the steric clashes it introduces, without destabilising the alpha-II tetramerization domain itself. The defect is therefore placed in alpha-II spectrin's binding to its beta partner. All of the support is computational; no binding assay on the mutant protein has been published.

nodes.description: A heterozygous missense or in-frame SPTAN1 variant at a residue that holds alpha-II spectrin's helices together. The SPG91 variants typically remove a positively charged arginine or lysine, or a hydrogen-bonding residue, at either the N-terminal tetramerization site or a position linking the three helices of a spectrin repeat. This distinguishes them both from the DEE5 variants, which are in-frame changes in the last two repeats, and from the truncating variants associated with hereditary motor neuropathy and distal myopathy. The role of these residues comes from structural modelling, not from biochemistry on the mutant protein.
